new_packages.label: טוֹב וּשְׁאִילַת תּוֹרָה — שָׁאוּל
new_packages.label_en: Inward Goodness and Concealed Torah — the Shaul Archetype
new_packages.reason: The source text explicitly establishes three concepts as bechinas of each other within the inward-containing tzaddik domain: (1) טוֹב — the Zohar quality of 'goodness entirely contained within itself' ('טוּבֵהּ כְּלִיל בְּגַוֵּהּ'); (2) שָׁאוּל — the named archetype of the non-revealing tzaddik ('שָׁאוּל דְּלָא גְּלֵי מַסֶּכְתָּא, זֶהוּ בְּחִינַת טוֹב'); (3) אֵינוֹ מְגַלֶּה תּוֹרָתוֹ לַאֲחֵרִים — the act of not-revealing, which is explicitly stated as the definition of the טוֹב quality. All three share the same essential nature: inward-directed, self-contained holiness that does not flow outward. This is not a cause-effect chain — Shaul is not the cause of the טוֹב quality; he is its human face, and not-revealing is its behavioral expression. The three are co-equal bechinas of the same underlying reality: holy energy that remains within its source rather than diffusing outward. This package is structurally required as the mirror of Package 1 (חסד/מגלה תורתו): just as the Zohar defines the two poles — טוֹב (inward) and חֶסֶד (outward) — Torah #283 structures its entire argument around this polarity. The dataset is missing all three edges for this domain (טוֹב ↔ שאול, טוֹב ↔ אינו מגלה, שאול ↔ אינו מגלה). The Rebbe's use of the Zohar source (Tikkun 168) as the structural backbone of the Torah makes this a primary conceptual package, not a peripheral addition.

שָׁאוּל דְּלָא גְּלֵי מַסֶּכְתָּא, זֶהוּ בְּחִינַת טוֹב, דְּטוּבֵהּ גְּנִיז בְּגַוֵּהּ

observations:
Torah #283 is architecturally concise: 3 bechina edges, 6 nodes, 3 connected components (all pairs). The dataset captures only half the teaching's conceptual structure.

The Torah's argument rests on a Zohar passage (Tikkun 168) that defines two qualities: טוֹב (goodness internally contained) and חֶסֶד (goodness flowing outward). These are the two poles of the Torah's entire discussion. The dataset captures the chesed pole (מגלה תורתו ↔ חסד, edge 1198) but has NO edges at all for the טוֹב pole — despite the Torah giving equal textual weight to both.

The source text makes three explicit bechina statements for the טוֹב domain:
1. 'זֶה בְּחִינַת טוֹב, שֶׁטּוּבֵהּ כְּלִיל בְּגַוֵּהּ' — the first tzaddik type IS bechina of tov
2. 'שָׁאוּל דְּלָא גְּלֵי מַסֶּכְתָּא, זֶהוּ בְּחִינַת טוֹב' — Shaul IS bechina of tov
3. 'שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְגַלֶּה תּוֹרָתוֹ לַאֲחֵרִים' — the action of not-revealing IS the defining bechina of tov

These three share the essential nature of 'contained, inward-radiating holiness' and form an independent domain that is the mirror-image of Package 1. Without this package, the good/evil structure of the Torah cannot be represented — though note that in this Torah neither pole is 'evil'; both are legitimate tzaddik qualities. The polarity of the new package is neutral because both archetypes are holy; the Torah frames the מחלקת as arising from the structural difference between them, not from one being good and the other evil.

Existing packages reviewed and found complete for their domains:
- Package 1 (חסד/מגלה תורתו): complete within the dataset — the only gap is the missing node דוד, which is an addition not a new package
- Package 2 (תורה/אש): complete as a pair — Torah-as-fire is the structural substrate that links all domains
- Package 3 (מחלקת/רעמים): complete as a pair — the structural metaphor is fully captured

The proposed Package 4 (טוֹב/שאול/אינו מגלה) requires 3 new dataset entries and meets the threshold of 3+ concepts connected by explicit bechina language forming an independent domain not covered by existing packages.
